content:
- Model consistently underestimates prices in the early part of the forecast horizon, especially after recent spikes.
- Overestimates near the end of the 30-day forecast, particularly when true values show upward momentum or mean reversion.
- Tends to lag behind true price movements, especially in the first 5–10 days of the forecast.
- Shows persistent bias toward lower values when historical mean is high (e.g., 70+), and overestimates when historical mean is low (e.g., 60–65).
- Overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., 68+ → 69+), then fails to correct downward in subsequent days.
- Mean reversion is not captured well — model holds onto overestimated values longer than actual price behavior suggests.
- Forecasts are overly conservative in volatile periods, underreacting to news or policy changes that drive price up.
- When true values rise sharply, model fails to anticipate the magnitude and timing, often underestimating the peak and overestimating the trough.
